d the prevention and control of marine pollution from ships, RECOGNIZING the need to reduce the environmental and occupational health and safety risks related to ship recycling and, at the same time, securing the smooth withdrawal of ships that have reached the end of their operating lives, RECOGNIZING ALSO the important role of the Organization in the regulation of ship recycling activity, and in coordinating its work on ship recycling matters with that of the International Labour Organization and the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal, NOTING that the Revised IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships adopted at the eightieth session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee will witness an increased phasing out of less efficient ships and hence an increased need for environmentally sound ship recycling facilities, CONSIDERING that the Hong Kong Convention will enter into force on 26 June 2025, CONCERNED t

ut of less efficient ships and hence an increased need for environmentally sound ship recycling facilities, CONSIDERING that the Hong Kong Convention will enter into force on 26 June 2025, CONCERNED that ships recycled in recycling fac ilities not complying with the requirements of safe and environmentally sound international measures for the recycling of ships could prevent international shipping from meeting its obligations to the 2030 United Nations Agenda for Sustainable Development, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT that many ship recycling facilities in Member States, particularly developing countries, are taking proactive efforts in line with their domestic legislation to improve existing recycling facilities including, where appropriate, through voluntary compliance with the Hong Kong Convention, and may be encouraged to verify their recycling facilities and recycling methodologies to be in line with the Hong Kong Convention, RESOLUTION A.1191(33) Adopted on 6 December 2023 (Agenda item 22)

ates undergo voluntary assessment for compliance with the Convention; 3 RECOMMENDS that Member Governments, especially the Governments of States with shipowning and registration interests, take initiatives, in cooperation with the shipping industry, to increase the number of ships re cycled at Hong Kong Convention-compliant ship recycling facilities. ___________ RESOLUTION A.1191(33) Adopted on 6 December 2023 (Agenda item 22) RESOLUTION FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE HONG KONG INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION FOR THE SAFE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND RECYCLING OF SHIPS, 2009 (THE HONG KONG CONVENTION) RESOLUTION A.1191(33) Adopted on 6 December 2023 (Agenda item 22) RESOLUTION FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE HONG KONG INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION FOR THE SAFE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND RECYCLING OF SHIPS, 2009 (THE HONG KONG CONVENTION)
